title: Potential geometrically reduced fibres of finite normalizations over a semilocal Dedekind base
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one with finitely many maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $(Z_i\to S)_{i\in I}$ be a finite family of separated flat finite-type schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Suppose each generic fibre $(Z_i)_K$ is geometrically normal: after every field extension of $K$ all its local rings are integrally closed domains. There is a finite field extension $L/K$ such that, writing $R_L$ for the integral closure of $R$ in $L$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R_L$, the componentwise normalizations $N_i=((Z_i\times_S T)_{\mathrm{red}})^\nu$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] have finite surjective canonical maps $N_i\to Z_i\times_S T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Each $N_i$ is normal, flat, separated and of finite type over $T$, and every field-valued fibre of $N_i\to T$ is geometrically reduced (reduced after every further field extension). The generic-fibre map $(N_i)_L\to (Z_i)_L$ is an isomorphism. The same extension $L$ works for every $i$. Empty schemes and empty fibres are allowed; no excellence or module-finiteness of $R_L/R$ is assumed.

source.place: Appendix II, Corollary 2, printed p.73 (Theorem 1 and its finite-type corollary). Apply Corollary 2 to the finite disjoint union of the Z_i for a simultaneous extension. Normality and the generic-fibre isomorphism are properties of normalization; separatedness follows from finiteness over the separated base change. Local archive WANTED; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1973__33__5_0.pdf

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/K$. Index by the finite intermediate fields $K\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$, a small nonempty directed set: the field generated by finitely many algebraic elements is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension]. Write $R_F$ for the integral closure of $R$ in $F$, and $B$ for its integral closure in $\Omega$. Every $b\in B$ belongs to some finite $F$, and its monic equation over $R$ is the same equation in $F$. Thus $B=\bigcup_FR_F=\varinjlim_FR_F$: compatible ring maps on these subrings glue by their common-stage formula. The affine schemes $S_F=\operatorname{Spec}R_F$ have limit $\operatorname{Spec}B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition].

source.place: Tags 09GH (lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated) and 01YW (limits.tex, lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit); explicit union of integral closures

proof.text: For every finite $F/K$, [lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres] makes $R_F$ a Noetherian normal domain of dimension one, with fraction field $F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal]. Also $\operatorname{Frac}B=\Omega$. The inclusion $R_F\subseteq B\subseteq\Omega$ is torsion-free, hence flat by [lem-sfb-dedekind-torsionfree-module-flat]. It is integral (the monic equations over $R$ are also equations over $R_F$), so lying over and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] make it faithfully flat. No finite-module assertion about $R_F/R$ has entered.

Choose a finite affine open cover of each $Z_i$, finitely many charts altogether since $I$ is finite and the morphisms are of finite type. Write a chart as $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its algebra is finite type over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], and finitely presented over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. Its generic fibre is geometrically normal: after any field extension it is an open subscheme of the given geometrically normal generic fibre, so its local rings have the stated property. For $A_F=A\otimes_RR_F$, base change preserves flatness and finite type. The algebra $A_F$ is Noetherian since it is finite type over $R_F$. It is reduced: flatness injects $A_F$ into $A\otimes_RF$, and that generic algebra is normal and therefore reduced. Explicitly, a nilpotent in $A_F$ maps to zero in the generic algebra, so injectivity kills it.

source.place: Tags 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), 00FP (finite type over Noetherian implies finite presentation), 01U9, 01T4 and 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); generic localization injectivity from flatness

proof.text: For each chart $A$, apply [lem-sfb-absolute-dedekind-normalization-reduced-fibres] to $R,A,\Omega$. All its hypotheses were verified in Step 3. It supplies the concrete integral closure $C\subseteq A_K\otimes_K\Omega$: $C$ is finite over $A_B$, flat and finitely presented over $B$, normal, with reduced geometric fibres and the specified generic-fibre isomorphism. This is the infinite algebraic-closure stage of Raynaud's argument, before choosing a finite field extension.

source.place: Appendix II Theorem 1, printed p.73; affine normalization over the algebraic closure

proof.text: By [lem-kun-fp-algebra-descent], descend $C$ as a finitely presented algebra $C_{F_0}$ over some $R_{F_0}$. The algebra $A_{F_0}$ is finitely presented, since it is finite type over the Noetherian ring $R_{F_0}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-category-fp-algebras] to descend the $B$-algebra map $A_B\to C$ to an $R_F$-algebra map $A_F\to C_F$ at a later stage. The prescribed comparison $C_F\otimes_{R_F}B\cong C$ identifies the base change of this map with the original map. All subsequent enlargements mean base change of these fixed models; the finite set of charts permits a common stage.

source.place: Tags 00QO (lemma-characterize-finite-presentation) and 05N9 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras); finitely presented algebra and map descent

proof.text: Enlarge $F$ so $A_F\to C_F$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-finite-ring-map], and $R_F\to C_F$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-flat-ring-map]. The first applies because $C_F$ is already finitely generated over $R_F$, hence over $A_F$; the second because $C_F$ is finitely presented over $R_F$. Apply [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-fibres-limit-descent] to $\operatorname{Spec}C_F\to\operatorname{Spec}R_F$ and the system $S_E$, $E\supseteq F$. The base schemes are affine qcqs, transitions affine, and the displayed morphism is of finite presentation. Its limit has reduced geometric fibres by Step 4. Hence enlarge again so this holds over $R_F$. Finite generation of the module persists by tensoring a finite generating family; flatness persists by flat base change. In particular these properties persist under further base change, in particular geometric reducedness by [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change].

source.place: Tags 07RG, 02JO(3), 0579, 0576 and 05F4; limits over finite normalized field stages

proof.text: The map $\operatorname{Spec}(C_F\otimes_{R_F}F)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A_K\otimes_KF)$ is of finite presentation: both algebras are finite type over the field, hence Noetherian, and the source algebra is finitely generated over the target algebra. Its base change to $\Omega$ is the generic-fibre isomorphism of Step 4. The fields $E\supseteq F$ have union $\Omega$, so their spectra have limit $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-limit-isomorphism-descent] to this inverse system to enlarge $F$ until the generic map itself is an isomorphism. Finite presentation over a field is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]; all sources and targets here are affine qcqs.

source.place: Tag 081E (limits.tex, lemma-descend-isomorphism); field inverse system, retaining the actual generic map

proof.text: The ring map $C_F\to C_F\otimes_{R_F}B\cong C$ is faithfully flat by Step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change]. Since $C$ is normal, [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-normal-ring-descent] proves that $C_F$ is normal. This remains true for every later stage: the map from that stage to the same ring $C$ is still faithfully flat. Thus the final common field may be chosen after all the preceding conditions for every chart, without any normality-persistence assumption under arbitrary base change.

Recognize $\operatorname{Spec}C_F$ as the componentwise normalization of $\operatorname{Spec}A_F$. Both are locally Noetherian, since $A_F$ and $C_F$ are finite type over $R_F$. Both are flat over $R_F$. By [lem-sc-flat-going-down], every minimal prime contracts to $(0)$: a prime properly above $(0)$ would admit a smaller prime by going down. Their component generic points therefore lie in the generic fibre. The generic-fibre isomorphism of Step 7 identifies these points bijectively and identifies their residue fields. The finite map is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], and the source is normal by Step 8. [lem-sfb-integral-normal-generic-recognition], applied to the locally Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A_F$, now gives its unique isomorphism with the componentwise normalization over $\operatorname{Spec}A_F$.

source.place: Tags 00HS (minimal primes under flat maps), 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral), 0H7D (recognition of normalization)

proof.text: Fix the one common finite stage $L$ just obtained for all charts of all $Z_i$. Set $T=\operatorname{Spec}R_L$ and $X_i=Z_i\times_ST$. Each $X_i$ is reduced by the generic-injectivity argument of Step 3; hence its reduction is itself. Each $X_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so its quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. By [lem-sfb-normalization-generic-residue-affine-charts], applied both to $X_i$ and to the affine chart $U_T=\operatorname{Spec}A_L$ itself (same generic points and residue fields), the restriction of $N_i=(X_{i,\mathrm{red}})^\nu$ to $U_T$ is $\operatorname{Spec}D_{U_T}$, i.e. the componentwise normalization of $U_T$, which is the one recognized in Step 9. It is therefore finite there, flat over $R_L$, and has geometrically reduced fibres. Finiteness is local for the Zariski covering of the target, as an instance of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite]; this open cover is an fpqc covering. Flatness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. Reducedness of a geometric fibre is checked on these open affine covers by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff]. By [lem-trf-affine-geometric-fibre-reduced-comparison], reducedness of the geometric fibre of a chart at $\mathfrak p$ means that its fibre over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is geometrically reduced; a fibre over any field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to E$ is that fibre tensored with $E$. Thus every field-valued fibre is geometrically reduced, including empty fibres.

source.place: Tags 035K (lemma-normalization-localization), 035P (morphisms.tex, lemma-description-normalization), 0BXC/0576 (geometric fibre reducedness), 02LA (descent.tex, lemma-descending-property-finite), 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), and 01J2 (schemes.tex, lemma-affine-reduced); affine covering assembly

proof.text: Each $N_i$ is normal and its canonical map to $X_i$ is surjective by [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-generic-properties], since $X_i$ is locally Noetherian (Step 10). The maps are finite by Step 10. Base change makes $X_i\to T$ separated and of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-separated-finite-type] therefore makes $N_i\to T$ separated and of finite type. The chartwise generic isomorphisms of Step 7 are the canonical normalization maps by Step 9 and hence give the claimed global generic-fibre isomorphism. If the family is empty or all charts are empty, take $L=K$; all conclusions are vacuous on empty schemes. Charts with empty special fibre require no change in the argument. This completes every clause with a single $L$, without excellence or module-finiteness of $R_L/R$.
